citation: Kaslow et al. (2018), Developing a CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) Reference Model - Interim Status #4
title: Developing a CubeSat Model-Based System Engineering (MBSE) Reference Model - Interim Status #4
venue_type: conference paper, American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA); exact conference name not reported in paper.md
modeling_scope: SysML CubeSat Reference Model for mission-specific CubeSat development. Scope includes stakeholder concerns, requirements, use cases, logical and physical architecture, CubeSat and ground subsystems/components, technical measures, table-based population workflows, OMG/XMI specification path, and a CRM validation strategy. Power is represented only generically through a Power Subsystem and planned power/weight/cost parametrics; no detailed EPS behavior model is reported in this paper.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML implemented in No Magic Cameo Systems Modeler/MagicDraw; CRM planned as SysML-compliant OMG XMI specification. Prior related phase mentioned Cameo Simulation Toolkit, Phoenix Integration ModelCenter/MBSE Analyzer, STK, and MATLAB.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite platform; general CRM for mission-specific CubeSat teams. Paper notes 1U and larger CubeSat form factors such as 3U, 6U, and 12U, and cites prior RAX CubeSat work.
task_domain: CubeSat systems engineering and reference-model development for mission-specific space/ground mission design; prior RAX example was an ionospheric science mission.
interface: Table-based user interfaces in Cameo Systems Modeler for adding, deleting, and modifying mission, specification, requirements, structures, and use-case information; XMI import/export interface for use across graphical modeling tools; embedded Word/Excel technical-measure method documents; trace/satisfy/verify/refine model relationships.
feedback: Technical-measure feedback loop in which verification activities provide data to assess MOEs/MOPs/TPMs, and parametric diagrams can support performance analysis. CRM validation also uses alpha-test CubeSat teams, debrief comments, metrics, and iterative engagement until confidence is reached or the approach is re-evaluated.
evaluation: Paper demonstrates the CRM by describing the Cameo implementation, packages, tables, stereotypes, and diagrams. It does not report a completed empirical evaluation; it presents a validation strategy using ten model-validation questions, expert preliminary validation, alpha testing by CubeSat teams, debriefs, and metrics. Current version had been shared with trusted partners and first alpha test arranged.
rq_relevance: RQ1: partial because the paper provides a general CubeSat MBSE reference model and generic Power Subsystem context, but not a detailed EPS model or EPS behavior abstraction. RQ2: partial because the paper claims reuse, traceability, analysis support, and model/tool integration from MBSE/CRM, but reports no measured reliability improvement and no EPS-specific reliability/reproducibility outcome. RQ3: partial because verification/validation is represented at the CRM/system level through requirement properties, verify relationships, technical-measure data, and CRM validation strategy, but EPS-specific verification procedures before hardware development are not described.
claimed_outcomes: CRM is intended as a reusable starting point for mission-specific CubeSat teams and as a repository for systems engineering artifacts.

Requirements and design are kept in the model rather than independent artifacts, supporting traceability among concerns, requirements, use cases, technical measures, architecture, satisfy, and verify relationships.
Technical measures traced from mission objectives to MOEs, MOPs, TPMs, and requirements support performance analysis and prediction of whether MOEs will be met.
OMG SysML-compliant XMI specification is intended to support import into different graphical modeling tools, improving model/tool interoperability.
The paper motivates MBSE by high CubeSat/university mission failure rates and need for rigorous systems engineering, but it does not report a quantified reliability improvement.
verification_validation_linkage: System-level linkage only. Requirement tables expose verify method and verified-by properties, and the paper states that proof of satisfy assertions is accomplished by verify relationships. Technical-measure assessment uses verification activity data. Section VI defines a CRM validation strategy using model-validation questions, SME review, alpha testing with CubeSat teams, debriefs, metrics, and iteration. No EPS-specific verification or physical test procedure model is reported.
key_findings: The CRM is a SysML, methodology-agnostic reference/template intended for CubeSat teams to import and specialize into mission-specific models.
The current maturation expands requirements and architecture packages down to CubeSat and ground subsystem/component levels and adds table-based population workflows.
The architecture decomposes the CubeSat mission into domain, enterprise, space segment, ground segment, CubeSat, CubeSat orbit, and subsystems including a Power Subsystem.
Use cases are modeled at enterprise, CubeSat, and CubeSat subsystem levels and can refine requirements through SysML relationships and linked description documents.

Technical measures are modeled from mission objectives to MOEs, MOPs, and TPMs, with traceability to requirements and optional implementation through constraint blocks, parametric diagrams, Word documents, or spreadsheets.
The CRM is being prepared as an OMG implementation-free XMI specification, with a Cameo implementation and web-published HTML as non-normative supporting material.
Validation is not completed; the paper presents a strategy requiring expert review and alpha testing with CubeSat teams using the CRM to build concrete mission-specific models.
Power, weight, and cost parametrics are identified as next steps rather than completed CRM capability in this interim paper.
limitations_gaps: The paper states that validating the CRM is difficult without concrete mission-specific models developed using the CRM.
CRM validation is still in progress: trusted partners had seen the current version and the first alpha test was arranged, but completed alpha-test evidence is not reported.
Power, weight, and cost parametrics are identified as future work, not as completed model content.
No EPS-specific verification procedure, EPS behavior model, or measured reliability/reproducibility outcome is reported in this paper.

quality.rationale: AIAA conference-style paper with DOI and AIAA footer supports venue credibility. The paper discusses validation difficulties and next-step gaps, but does not present a formal threats-to-validity section or completed empirical validation.
